cards.text: Paul, the apostle, is writing a letter to the church in Corinth (1 Corinthians 1:1-2). He just asked them whether they want him to come with a rod, or in love and with a gentle spirit (1 Corinthians 4:21). Now he turns to a report about them: a man among them has his father's wife, a kind of sexual immorality that is intolerable even among pagans.

cards.question: A man in the Corinthian church has his father's wife. How does Paul say the Corinthians are acting about it?

cards.text: Paul says they should have been stricken with grief instead.

cards.question: Paul says the church should have removed the man who has his father's wife from their ___.

cards.text: Paul isn't in Corinth, but he says he's present with them in spirit. That's the exact OPPOSITE of a Monday morning: body at work, spirit still back on the snooze button.

cards.question: Paul says he'll wait until he gets to Corinth to pronounce judgment on the man who has his father's wife.

cards.text: When they're assembled in the name of the Lord Jesus, with Paul there in spirit and the power of the Lord Jesus, they're to hand this man over to Satan for the destruction of the flesh. That's heavy, friend, but Paul gives a reason.

cards.question: Paul says the man is handed over to Satan so that his spirit may be ___ on the Day of the Lord.

cards.text: Paul tells them their boasting is not good. Then he pulls an example straight out of the KITCHEN, and friend, I just hopped so high my gold base left the ground.

cards.question: Paul says a little leaven works through the whole batch of dough.

cards.text: So Paul says to get rid of the old leaven, so they can be a new unleavened batch, as they really are. Out it goes, like the dough I kept saying I'd use "tomorrow" for THREE weeks.

cards.question: Paul says Christ has been sacrificed. Which feast's lamb does Paul call Christ?

cards.text: So Paul says let's keep the feast, but not with the old bread, leavened with malice and wickedness. Friend, you could pour EVERY sprinkle in my bakery on that loaf and it still wouldn't help.

cards.question: The old bread is leavened with malice and wickedness. What does Paul say the unleavened bread for the feast is of?

cards.text: Next, Paul brings up an earlier letter where he told the Corinthians not to associate with sexually immoral people. Now he spells out what he meant, like that second text everybody's sent that starts "Okay, let me explain."

cards.question: Paul meant the Corinthians should stay away from every sexually immoral person in the world.

cards.text: Paul says he wasn't including the sexually immoral, the greedy, swindlers or idolaters of this world, or they'd have to leave this world. Friend, it took an ANGEL to get me out of one junk drawer.

cards.question: Paul's earlier letter said not to associate with sexually immoral people. Who does Paul now say he means?

answers.text: Anyone who claims to be a brother but is immoral or greedy
Anyone who claims to be a brother but follows Apollos
Anyone who claims to be a brother but was never baptized

cards.text: Paul names exactly who he means: anyone who claims to be a brother but is sexually immoral or greedy, an idolater or a verbal abuser, a drunkard or a swindler.

cards.question: Paul says that with someone who claims to be a brother but is sexually immoral or greedy, an idolater or a verbal abuser, a drunkard or a swindler, do not even ___ with him.

cards.text: Then Paul asks what business it is of his to judge those outside the church, and whether the Corinthians aren't to judge those inside. Kind of like how I scrub my OWN counters every night and have never once flown off this planet to scrub somebody else's.

cards.question: Paul says God will judge those outside the church.
Paul ends with a command for the church about the wicked man. What is it?

answers.text: Pray for him day and night
Send him to Paul at once
